title: Mosaic Selections recommendations for explorEDA
status: Research recommendations only; no application implementation or application/runtime/performance tests executed.
decision: Keep the existing React/TypeScript/Crossfilter stack. Selectively use Mosaic's model for a bounded exact four-consumer proof. Do not adopt Mosaic dependencies, optimizer, DuckDB interaction backend or renderers in the first experiment.

evidence_statuses.observed_repo: Static repository source at the pinned explorEDA baseline; inspected tests are specifications, not passes.
evidence_statuses.current_upstream: Static official implementation/documentation at the separate pinned Mosaic revision.
evidence_statuses.paper_claim: Claim or algorithm condition in arXiv:2507.19690v1.
evidence_statuses.inference_unrun: Source-derived reasoning or candidate counterexample not exercised in the application.
evidence_statuses.assignment_constraint: Explicit instruction or product boundary in the supplied assignment.

proof_gate_note: All gates below are proposed/unrun. Requirements are descriptive; semantic S- and optional acceleration A- identifiers may be cross-referenced by the final proof plan without changing their meaning.

recommendations.title: Retain React, TypeScript, existing renderers and Crossfilter for the first proof
recommendations.problem: The immediate need is consistent exact selection across existing consumers. Introducing a new backend, renderer or dependency before proving that need would add migration work without repairing the current semantic seams.
affected_workflow: Existing chart interaction and exact evidence

evidence.locator: prompt.md: Verified local starting facts; Ranked questions 2 and 5
evidence.claim: The assignment requires preserving React/TypeScript, using pnpm, keeping the personal-project design direct, and making the first milestone useful without a backend replacement.
The existing engine already owns independent chart dimensions, workspace field predicates and exact filtered row IDs.
Existing shared hooks distinguish live/context IDs from all rows in a chart population.

evidence.locator: docs/web-clients/index.md: React useEffect/makeClient example at pinned Mosaic revision
evidence.claim: React can also be retained if a later backend adoption is justified; a renderer/framework rewrite is not a prerequisite.

recommendations.proposed_change: Make the first implementation dependency-free with respect to Mosaic and DuckDB: retain the existing stack and selectively use the paper's source-owned clause and target-resolution ideas. Preserve existing chart plans, trace readers and embedding behavior. Treat no adoption of Mosaic packages, optimizer and rendering ecosystem as the current decision.
recommendations.benefit: Concentrates work on user-visible correctness, keeps the proof reviewable, and preserves current embedding and rendering behavior.
recommendations.cost: Low architectural cost for retaining the stack; bounded work remains in semantic adapters, affected consumers and verification. No schedule, bundle-size or speed estimate is asserted.

impact.exactness: Can improve agreement without changing the data engine, provided consumer-specific predicates and scopes are explicitly audited.
impact.performance: No speedup is promised; existing hot paths remain measurable in the same engine.
impact.public_api: Keep the initial contract internal. Existing exported settings and save semantics remain the compatibility baseline.

recommendations.alternative: Adopt a Mosaic Selection adapter or a Mosaic/DuckDB interaction backend later only if interoperability or measured query costs make the additional translation worthwhile.

confidence.basis: The current repository already supplies the core filtering, identity and evidence paths needed for a bounded proof.
confidence.caveat: This is an architectural recommendation, not an executed implementation or performance comparison.

requirements: Complete the four-consumer semantic proof using existing React/TypeScript renderers and Crossfilter.
Preserve legacy saved settings, exact evidence, clear/undo/restore and host callback behavior.
Record whether the internal contract provides a concrete benefit before reconsidering dependencies.
stop_conditions: Stop if the proof requires an unresolved backend or public-API migration to establish basic exact membership.

recommendations.title: Reconcile numeric histogram and Scatter marginal interval boundaries
recommendations.problem: Interior numeric bins use half-open membership, but selecting them can emit a range whose shared evaluator includes both endpoints. A boundary row can therefore enter linked evidence even though it belongs to the adjacent displayed bin.
affected_workflow: Linked table, finding, metric and trace agreement

evidence.claim: Bin partitioning closes only the terminal bin, while the selection writer emits min/max ranges without closure metadata.
The shared numerical range predicate accepts values greater than or equal to min and less than or equal to max.
Marginal bin assignment and emitted range filters have the same boundary-policy seam.

evidence.locator: Source-derived counterexample using x=[0,0.5,1] with two fractional bins
evidence.claim: The first bin contains only x=0, while its emitted closed [0,0.5] range also matches x=0.5. This is an unexecuted static counterexample.

recommendations.proposed_change: Reproduce the counterexample in the full checkout, then represent interval inclusivity explicitly for bin selections or use exact revision-bound contributor IDs where that is the intended durable meaning. Preserve the existing inclusive meaning of manually entered 'at most' ranges and old saves. Do not repair boundaries with an arbitrary epsilon. Apply the same rule to histogram and marginal writers.
recommendations.benefit: Makes the selected mark, linked evidence and reported count refer to the same records at internal and terminal bin edges.
recommendations.cost: Small, bounded semantic correction across interval representation/evaluation, the affected writers, persistence validation if extended, and targeted membership tests; a public range-shape change requires review.

impact.exactness: Corrects a concrete source-derived membership discrepancy; terminal-edge, open-range and date semantics must remain explicit.
impact.performance: Expected membership-evaluation cost remains small, but no performance result has been measured.
impact.public_api: If optional closure fields are added, legacy ranges must keep their existing inclusive default and old files must remain valid.

recommendations.alternative: For a limited proof, select exact contributor IDs scoped to the current data revision; defer the general interval extension until durable value-range intent is required.

confidence.basis: The partition and evaluator mismatch is directly visible in the inspected source.
confidence.caveat: No UI reproduction or application test was executed; verify the proposed correction before shipping.

requirements: With x=[0,0.5,1] and two bins, assert the first bin's selected IDs contain only the x=0 record.
Assert just-below, exact-edge, just-above and final-edge rows match displayed bin contributors, table/export IDs and finding count.
Repeat through brush, marginal selection, save/restore and bin-setting changes; retain old inclusive-range behavior.
stop_conditions: Stop on any selected-ID mismatch or silent reinterpretation of old saved ranges.

recommendations.title: Introduce a small internal exact contract owned by selection sources
recommendations.problem: A Filter[] has different interpretations in different chart definitions, and source identity, target exclusion, scope and persistent meaning are not one explicit contract. Simply sharing an object or appending arbitrary filters would preserve those inconsistencies.
affected_workflow: One gesture shared by histogram, scatterplot, evidence table and finding
Two charts selecting the same field
Clear one source, source-self-filtering and exact evidence

evidence.claim: Chart definitions consume their saved filters differently; the shared array type alone does not guarantee common evaluation.
The repository already has source-separated chart dimensions and independent workspace constraints.
Pinned Mosaic source demonstrates source-owned clauses and target-specific exclusion, with a separate update-skip mechanism.
Upstream clauses carry runtime object/client/SQL-AST references; they are not directly a serializable stable provenance model.

recommendations.proposed_change: Prototype one small internal serializable predicate contract with view-scoped stable source identity, data revision, typed semantic values, explicit interval closure, a bounded geometry kind and target resolution. Keep pixels, active handles and preview scheduling transient. Reuse existing parsers and primitive filter evaluation where sound; preserve legacy chart-definition behavior through explicit adapters. Default to intersection across independent sources, and represent exact correlated tuples only when needed rather than flattening them into independent field lists.
recommendations.benefit: Gives multiple consumers the same exact semantic selection while allowing a source chart to display context excluding itself.
recommendations.cost: Moderate, bounded integration work in source writers, a resolver, affected consumers, validation and lifecycle tests. Avoid a plugin framework, SQL parser or general query language.

impact.exactness: Provides a shared place to state and prove exact membership, empty-versus-cleared state and per-target scope.
impact.performance: May remove redundant semantic work, but no speedup is established; it does not itself implement Mosaic materialized views.
impact.public_api: Start internal. Persisted extensions require a reviewed version/validation decision; expose no general public selection API until a real embedding need emerges.

recommendations.alternative: Retain current settings and document their contracts, with direct fixes and a narrowly shared resolver only for the selected-count proof.

confidence.basis: Source-specific dimensions and exact ID paths already exist, while concrete consumers reveal the value of explicit resolution.
confidence.caveat: The smallest useful shape and its maintenance advantage remain to be proved in the bounded experiment.

requirements: Prove two independent sources selecting the same field can replace or clear their own clause without erasing the other.
Prove source-self-filtering on/off and source context versus exact evidence using the declared truth table.
Reject unknown fields or stale references visibly; distinguish no clause from an active predicate with zero matches.
Compare exact stable IDs across all four consumers, trace and export after each committed revision.
stop_conditions: Stop if any adapter ignores a guard, widens a scope, loses provenance or needs an unresolved general architecture.

recommendations.title: Prove an exact lasso on linear numeric Scatter axes with four consumers
recommendations.problem: A rectangular interval proof would not establish the precise-selection intent's requested lasso behavior. A polygon must preserve exact source-row membership, including points inside its bounding box but outside the polygon.

evidence.claim: The current intent explicitly prioritizes a small lasso proof, with boundary behavior, before broader composite selection work.
Existing Scatter plans retain source/live/selected row identities and supply the exact membership/evidence foundation.
The inspected Region/2D interaction is rectangular and does not implement the requested freeform polygon lasso.
The inspected optimizer recognizes point/interval metadata; an arbitrary polygon does not automatically gain acceleration.

recommendations.proposed_change: Build a proposed, bounded lasso proof only for linear numeric axes. Store polygon vertices in source units, define boundary inclusion once, exclude invalid coordinates, and evaluate the full eligible source population rather than only rendered/sampled points. Drive histogram, scatterplot, evidence table and one written count from the same committed selection. Use a rectangle as a comparison case, not completion of the lasso goal.
recommendations.benefit: Directly tests the user's highest-priority precise-selection benefit with visible evidence and a small, understandable interaction.
recommendations.cost: Moderate, bounded geometry, gesture, cancellation, keyboard-equivalent and four-consumer wiring work; defer transformed axes and broad gesture tooling.

impact.exactness: Requires a true point-in-polygon membership oracle, explicit boundaries and equality through resize, trace and export.
impact.performance: Full-row polygon evaluation may be a visible cost and must be measured; no optimizer benefit is assumed.
impact.public_api: Keep the first geometry shape internal and serializable; expand supported axes or external APIs only after this proof succeeds.

recommendations.alternative: Use an exact row-ID selection fixture to establish consumer wiring first, while leaving the lasso milestone explicitly incomplete.

confidence.basis: The intent and existing exact Scatter plans support a focused experiment.
confidence.caveat: Geometry UX, keyboard operation and end-to-end latency remain unrun product checks.

requirements: Use a nonrectangular polygon with at least one fixture point inside the bounding box but outside the polygon, plus boundary, duplicate-coordinate and invalid-coordinate cases.
Verify declared source-self-filtering on/off, a second competing selection, zero rows, clear, undo/redo, save/restore, trace and complete CSV equality.
Verify resize changes only display geometry, not source-space membership.
Provide a meaningful keyboard alternative and cancellation path at wide, intermediate and narrow widths.
stop_conditions: Stop if a rectangle or pixel/raster overlap replaces polygon membership, if contributors are lost, or if boundary semantics remain unresolved.

recommendations.title: Keep DataTable filtering coherent when a filtered column is hidden
recommendations.problem: The table's local row filter applies all saved filters, but its linked chart predicate ignores a filter once the field is absent from visible columns. Hiding presentation can therefore produce different populations in the table and siblings.
affected_workflow: Filter a dashboard table, then hide or drag away that column

evidence.claim: The linked predicate returns true for an individual filter when its field has no matching visible column.
Local filtering still evaluates saved filters; hiding a column changes columns without clearing the predicate.
updateChart shallow-merges changed settings and rebuilds the chart predicate.

evidence.locator: Static filter-then-hide sequence across the cited local and linked paths
evidence.claim: The two populations can diverge after the same saved settings update. This candidate behavior was not executed in the UI.

recommendations.proposed_change: Reproduce the filter-then-hide sequence. Prefer making predicate membership independent of column visibility and exposing the still-active filter in scope controls. If product review instead chooses to clear a hidden field filter, clear it atomically in both local and linked state. Preserve the intentionally table-local nature of globalSearch.
recommendations.benefit: Prevents a presentation edit from silently changing linked analytical meaning and makes exported table evidence explainable.
recommendations.cost: Small, bounded change in the table predicate/column action plus one end-to-end membership regression and clear/history verification.

impact.exactness: Restores agreement for the same declared table scope; it must not erase legitimate differences caused by table-local search.
impact.performance: No significant benefit is claimed; a retained predicate has the same general filtering work.
impact.public_api: Can likely retain the current saved shape; the visible-filter retention or atomic-clear behavior must be documented.

recommendations.alternative: Clear the affected column filter whenever the column is hidden, with an explicit scope update and a reversible history step.

confidence.basis: The inconsistent gates are directly visible in source.
confidence.caveat: The preferred retention behavior is a product proposal; runtime reproduction remains unrun.

requirements: Filter a visible column, record stable IDs in table/siblings/CSV, hide the column, and assert the chosen retained-or-cleared policy everywhere.
Undo/redo and restore the hidden-column state without a silent population change.
Verify table-only globalSearch still narrows only that table and its CSV.
stop_conditions: Stop if local and linked membership differ without an explicitly declared local restriction.

recommendations.title: Add one explicit selected-count binding to an authored finding
recommendations.problem: Daily findings use a separate static condition evaluator, while ordinary Markdown stores authored HTML. Neither establishes that written findings currently follow workspace selection. Reusing the daily evaluator unchanged would create coercion, missingness and zero-row differences.
affected_workflow: Select rows and read the written result
Inspect the records supporting a finding
Clear, restore and edit authored notes

evidence.claim: Static findings have their own comparison/coercion rules, denominator handling and a throw on empty/nonfinite results.
Corpus tests check formatted computed statements against local published data, not a live workspace-selection subscription.
The intended next increment is a bounded selected count, not generated narrative or a template language.
Existing metric behavior supplies a compatibility reference for selected-row count and future measure contributors.

recommendations.proposed_change: Prototype one authored selected-result-row count binding with explicit workspace scope, stable binding ID, numeric format and an inspect action. Resolve it from the same coherent exact population as the metric/evidence consumer; render zero as 0 and stale/incompatible scope as unavailable. Persist the definition and authored content, not evaluated HTML, row caches or every brush preview. Leave daily findings on their existing authored-corpus path.
recommendations.benefit: A written claim becomes inspectable and stays synchronized with the selected records without introducing a general narrative system.
recommendations.cost: Small-to-moderate bounded settings/rendering/inspection work and lifecycle checks; an editor token is optional if a dedicated finding consumer is simpler.

impact.exactness: The finding must name its population; future measures need separate valid-contributor and denominator semantics. The first workspace finding denominator is D∩W; existing MetricCard uses a full-source/local baseline excluding W. Compare count numerators unless denominators are explicitly aligned.
impact.performance: Count evaluation should reuse the current resolved population where sound; no independent daily condition scan or speed guarantee is proposed.
impact.public_api: Add only a bounded persisted binding shape after review. Do not expose arbitrary expressions, code or report templates.

recommendations.alternative: Use the existing count metric card alongside static notes and defer dynamic narrative until the proof demonstrates a workflow advantage.

confidence.basis: The narrative intent is explicit and the static/live semantic gap is visible in source.
confidence.caveat: The best minimal authoring UI and inspection presentation remain design choices to validate.

requirements: Verify finding count, metric count and exact table/export IDs agree for normal, zero-row, clear and competing-source cases.
Inspect the finding's complete declared population; label any Rows-local search/filter rather than silently narrowing its evidence.
Verify save/restore, undo/redo, note editing and view duplication retain the binding without storing runtime values as authored edits.
For any later percentage, define a safe denominator and show unavailable when it is zero.
stop_conditions: Stop if a statement is stale, implies a different denominator, uses an independent predicate meaning, or generates history entries for each rendered value.

recommendations.title: Close persistence, logical identity and typed DSL gaps before shipping rich predicates
recommendations.problem: New geometry or source references would pass through validators, logical-key adapters, field-usage checks, clear/reset paths, history and text export. Existing traversals cover only current shapes, and workspace DSL value resolution has a source-derived mixed-type ambiguity.
affected_workflow: Duplicate/delete chart or view and undo/restore

evidence.claim: Persisted validation admits the four existing filters, workspace fields are unique, and migration is currently a no-op.
Existing logical-key adaptation covers chart.filters and Rows filters for value/__ID, not every predicate container.
Value resolution uses String(raw) keys; workspace filters can be omitted, while charts have additional generic-difference fallback and chart IDs can be renamed.
View duplication retains inner chart IDs under a new view ID; undo and restore reconstruct snapshots.

evidence.locator: Mixed numeric/string or boolean/string category workspace roundtrip
evidence.claim: The String-key lookup can retarget a value to the first colliding type. This is an unexecuted source-derived candidate issue, not a demonstrated failure of every chart roundtrip.

recommendations.proposed_change: Before any rich predicate ships, inventory and extend the existing save/restore, logical-key and field-dependency traversals; scope source identity to view/workspace; validate data revisions and unresolved fields; clear/copy/dispose state deliberately. Reproduce and correct mixed-type workspace DSL roundtrips. Support faithful JSON first, and make unsupported DSL exports explicit rather than approximating or dropping membership silently. Keep legacy saves valid.
recommendations.benefit: Selections remain about the same records after restore, reorder, duplication and text exchange, and unsupported paths cannot silently widen the analysis.
recommendations.cost: Moderate, bounded cross-cutting work across known persistence and identity seams; this is a prerequisite gate, not a request for speculative compatibility infrastructure.

impact.exactness: Prevents positional-ID retargeting, lost guards, typed-value collisions and unresolved-reference widening.
impact.performance: Validation and restoration have setup cost that must be measured separately; no interaction-speed benefit is assumed.
impact.public_api: Saved schema/DSL changes are observable compatibility changes. Add explicit validation/version handling and preserve existing serialized meaning.

recommendations.alternative: Keep the first geometry experiment transient and nonexportable with a clear limitation, while retaining current supported saved predicates until the lifecycle proof is complete.

confidence.basis: The required traversal boundaries and text representation differences are directly visible in source and inspected identity tests.
confidence.caveat: Mixed-type DSL behavior and the proposed extended lifecycle are unrun checks; do not claim all existing exports are lossy.

requirements: Roundtrip old and new JSON settings and compare exact IDs and source references, including open bounds and empty-versus-cleared state.
Reorder related-table source rows and verify existing logical row keys remain stable; remove a selected row and ensure it never retargets another position.
Exercise chart/view duplication, deletion, clear-all, type/calculation edits, data replacement, undo/redo and checkpoint restore.
Roundtrip number 1 versus string 1 and boolean true versus string true through workspace and chart DSL with reversed fixture order; inspect all omissions/diagnostics.
Verify source-reference remapping when text export normalizes chart handles.
stop_conditions: Stop on membership/provenance loss, silent unsupported export, unresolved fields treated as all rows, or incompatible old-save reinterpretation.

recommendations.title: Preserve parsers, population rules, entity reducers and delivered density/Heatmap behavior
recommendations.problem: A selection refactor or SQL-style simplification could accidentally change typed categories, numeric/date parsing, missingness, entity-aware measures, source domains or recently delivered Heatmap histories.
affected_workflow: Compare charts and explain missing/invalid/zero values
Read count, sum and average with entity semantics
Inspect Scatter density and complete Heatmap histories

evidence.locator: packages/explorEDA/src/lib/valueParsing.ts; typed category helpers referenced by applyFilter
evidence.claim: The repository already defines deliberate numeric, category and UTC date semantics.
Chart-local populations are distinct from outgoing interactive predicates.
Reducers retain valid-measure exclusions and entity/conflict semantics that cannot be replaced blindly with row counts or averages of averages.
Delivered density uses source-unit bins, exact sourceIds and a full-source reference maximum.
Delivered Heatmap behavior includes complete date histories, exact period selection and configurable fixed color endpoints/sqrt mapping; automatic domains still follow shown cells.
The delivery section records the PR #450 improvements and supersedes earlier pending-plan descriptions.

recommendations.proposed_change: Use existing parsers, effective-field data and entity-aware reducers as the semantic baseline. Preserve local populations and full-source encodings where already implemented. Retain delivered Scatter density evidence and PR #450 Heatmap history/fixed-end behavior. Add focused regressions around the new selection path; do not reopen unrelated completed chart work or assert that Heatmap's automatic domain is already globally fixed.
recommendations.benefit: Protects analytical meaning and recently completed user-visible behavior while the shared contract is introduced.
recommendations.cost: Low-to-moderate preservation and targeted regression effort; avoid a simultaneous reducer, parsing or chart redesign.

impact.exactness: Keeps invalid dates, blank measures, absent periods, true zero and entity contributions distinct.
impact.performance: Existing caches and reducers remain the baseline. Any alternative must measure equivalent work and semantics.
impact.public_api: No unnecessary parser/reducer API expansion or change to existing chart settings is required.

recommendations.alternative: Introduce a separately reviewed normalization or aggregate backend only after full semantic parity is demonstrated for the relevant data types and entity rules.

confidence.basis: The delivered behaviors and source semantics are explicit at the pinned baseline.
confidence.caveat: Regression tests were inspected, not executed during this research.

requirements: Verify typed categories, numeric-string intervals, UTC/offset boundaries, invalid dates, missing buckets and true zero cases.
Verify member rows versus valid numeric contributors, entity deduplication and conflict/unavailable results.
Verify linked selection keeps Scatter density reference meaning and configured Heatmap color endpoints stable.
Run the delivered complete-history Heatmap and density regressions without converting them into new feature work.
stop_conditions: Stop if a new resolver changes analytical meaning or turns a missing/unavailable value into a valid zero.

recommendations.title: Measure a production interaction baseline before introducing acceleration
recommendations.problem: The repository records residual interaction cost, but its historical development-build long-task totals are not production p50/p95 latency or evidence that filtering is the dominant bottleneck. Faster predicates may leave ID materialization, chart plans, traces and rendering unchanged.
affected_workflow: Source switching, restore and data/calculation edits
Exact evidence queries and export after interaction

evidence.locator: docs/performance-checks.md: measurement guidance, production-build guidance, message-log and January-flights tables
evidence.claim: Historical numbers name their development build and long-task method; several expensive paths are already fixed at the baseline.
Live-data publication fans out across chart groups and local populations; workspace columns are already read once when predicates are compiled.
Predicate updates, column caches, derived-field changes and publication are distinct measurable stages.
Even the upstream query system manages fan-out, concurrency, deduplication and cache lifecycle; query acceleration alone is not the whole user-visible path.

recommendations.proposed_change: Run the proof plan's small reproducible production benchmark against the immutable baseline and the bounded candidate. Declare hardware, browser, build, row counts/distributions, chart count and interaction traces. Measure cold setup, warm p50/p95 interaction-to-coherent-display, exact evidence latency, memory, source switching and invalidation. Separate predicate commit, IDs, plan/reducer and rendering costs. Proceed to optimization only for an identified bottleneck.
recommendations.benefit: Makes a later performance decision attributable, reproducible and honest about setup and exact-evidence cost.
recommendations.cost: Bounded benchmark/instrumentation work using existing repository tooling; no schedule or numerical speedup estimate is supplied.

impact.exactness: Exact stable row-ID equality is a hard gate for every timed candidate; aggregate tolerance cannot excuse membership differences.
impact.performance: Produces evidence of whether optimization is needed and where; it is not itself a promise of faster interactions.
impact.public_api: Temporary instrumentation and an external proof harness need no public API. Remove diagnostic product code before integration.

recommendations.alternative: Ship only the semantic correction if measured performance is adequate, retaining the current caches and renderer behavior.

confidence.basis: The source exposes multiple plausible costs and existing performance docs require measured, build-qualified claims.
confidence.caveat: No explorEDA benchmark was run in this research; published paper speedups are not substituted.

requirements: Report cold and warm setup/query/interaction distributions, memory and exact-evidence latency on declared representative workloads.
Include one/two-dimensional predicates, repeated commits, competing sources, chart fan-out, skew/high cardinality, restore and calculated-field/data invalidation.
Compare exact IDs before accepting any timing result and disclose how many trials and which build were used.
Identify a repeatable dominant cost before proposing a cache or backend change.
stop_conditions: Stop a candidate benchmark on membership/provenance mismatch; defer acceleration if benefit is absent, too small to justify complexity, or dominated by unchanged rendering work.

recommendations.title: Defer a Mosaic Selection adapter until interoperability earns its cost
recommendations.problem: The Selection library can be used without a running coordinator, but it does not eliminate explorEDA's need for stable persisted identities, JavaScript predicate evaluation, target populations and React lifecycle management. Two semantic representations can drift.

evidence.claim: Selection has runtime source identity, reset/remove semantics and an undefined update-skip result that must not be treated as all rows.
Clauses contain object identity, client Sets and SQL expression nodes requiring translation for durable explorEDA state.
The inspected core manifest has SQL, DuckDB-WASM and related dependencies and no advertised selection-only subpath; no bundle-size measurement was performed.
The host already has its own logical-key and restore boundary that an adapter must respect.

recommendations.proposed_change: Do not add Mosaic Selection to the first experiment. Keep a later adapter decision conditional on a real Mosaic interoperability workflow or a separately justified database backend. If revisited, use a thin translation from one authoritative serializable semantic representation, with stable runtime source objects, subscription cleanup and explicit context/evidence resolution.
recommendations.benefit: Avoids dependency and lifecycle complexity while retaining a concrete path to interoperability if it becomes useful.
recommendations.cost: No adapter implementation cost now. A later bounded spike must assess translation, cleanup, persistence, API stability and measured dependency/bundle impact; no byte estimate is asserted.

impact.exactness: Deferral avoids a second independent predicate interpretation; a future adapter must prove typed, interval, tuple and skip-sentinel parity.
impact.performance: Selection adoption alone does not provide database materialization speedups.
impact.public_api: No new external selection types or Mosaic objects enter the current public API or saved format.

recommendations.alternative: Continue the small internal contract indefinitely if it meets the workflow; adopt only the model and document that no-library outcome.

confidence.basis: Official APIs establish feasibility but also concrete translation obligations; the first proof does not require Mosaic interoperability.
confidence.caveat: No adapter was built and no bundle or runtime lifecycle measurement was performed.

requirements: Reopen only with a named interoperability/backend requirement and a bounded comparison against the internal contract.
Verify source-self-filtering, clear/remove/reset, no-clause versus false predicate, undefined skip sentinel, React cleanup and restore.
Measure actual dependency/bundle impact and maintenance surface before adopting.
stop_conditions: Stop if the adapter creates competing authoritative semantics, silently converts update-skip to all rows, or cannot dispose/rebuild stable sources correctly.

recommendations.title: Defer a Mosaic/DuckDB optimizer backend pending measured need and exact parity
recommendations.problem: The optimizer analyzes structured SQL and materializes database tables; scale metadata cannot make it accelerate arbitrary Crossfilter reducers. Backend adoption would migrate schema, queries, identities, aggregates and async evidence lifecycle.
affected_workflow: Cold start, active-source switching and materialized-view reuse
Exact evidence after data or calculation changes

evidence.claim: The paper's materialized-view approach depends on compatible workloads, dimensions, sufficient measures and construction/storage costs; its evaluated gains are conditional paper claims.
Current materialization is active-source and client-query specific and requires eligible metadata.
Eligibility depends on structured stable aggregate queries and recognized relation/aggregate forms.

evidence.locator: packages/mosaic/core/src/preagg/sufficient-statistics.ts: supported aggregate dispatch and weighted average/non-null count
evidence.claim: Sufficient-statistic support is operation-specific; it is not arbitrary median/distinct/entity-reducer acceleration.
Existing entity and exclusion semantics require explicit backend parity.

recommendations.proposed_change: Do not adopt DuckDB or Mosaic preaggregation as the first interaction backend. Reconsider only after the production baseline isolates a query/aggregation bottleneck. A later prototype must translate a small supported consumer set, preserve exact IDs and reducer meaning, measure construction/cold/warm/memory costs, and invalidate both result caches and materialized tables on data/field revision changes.
recommendations.benefit: Prevents an expensive migration driven by attractive benchmark numbers while preserving a realistic option for sufficiently large repeated analytical workloads.
recommendations.cost: High relative to the bounded internal proof: consumer query migration, normalization, identities, async lifecycle, cache invalidation and operational tests. Defer this cost until evidence justifies it.

impact.exactness: Requires row-level parity, correct valid-measure denominators, entity semantics and fail-safe fallback for unsupported queries.
impact.performance: Potentially useful for repeated compatible queries, but construction/cardinality/memory/source-switch costs can outweigh gains; no explorEDA speedup is claimed.
impact.public_api: A backend abstraction and new dependencies would expand maintenance and embedding behavior substantially; keep that decision separate.

recommendations.alternative: Optimize a measured Crossfilter or chart-plan hot path directly, retaining exact source-row evaluation and existing renderers.

confidence.basis: The inspected optimizer has concrete SQL and compatibility requirements not present in generic Crossfilter reducers.
confidence.caveat: The future workload benefit is unknown because no candidate backend benchmark was run here.

requirements: Require a measured bottleneck and declare the small supported query/aggregate workload before prototyping.
Verify exact IDs and aggregate contributor semantics with optimization enabled/disabled and across cold/warm/source-switch cases.
Measure construction time, sparse/dense cardinality effects, memory, transfer/render costs and exact evidence latency.
Invalidate data revision, calculated-field changes, result caches and materialized state independently; verify unchanged SQL over changed rows is fresh.
stop_conditions: Stop on parity failure, unsupported reducer approximation or stale evidence; defer if amortized benefit does not exceed measured setup and maintenance costs.

recommendations.title: Reject pixel membership and unsupported union acceleration as exact evidence
recommendations.problem: An exact aggregate over quantized bins can still select different source rows than the original predicate. The paper also excludes UNION from its materialized-view compatibility, while the inspected upstream path has no explicit union-resolution guard.
affected_workflow: Combining multiple nonempty sources with union

evidence.claim: The inspected optimizer can quantize source values before interval filtering; no explicit UNION guard was found in the audited path.
The interval inversion helper snaps screen coordinates to its pixel-size grid.
The v1 algorithm limits this optimization to INTERSECT or LAST rather than UNION.

evidence.locator: Static example: source [10,20] versus floor(x) BETWEEN 10 AND 20 with x=20.9; general union composition
evidence.claim: Quantization can admit a nonmember, and materializing other clauses then filtering the active clause does not implement general union. These are unexecuted source-derived concerns, not reproduced upstream bugs.

recommendations.proposed_change: Keep exact source-space predicates authoritative for table/export/trace/finding membership. Permit a coarse preview only with explicit preview semantics and exact candidate rechecking or boundary-bin evaluation before final evidence. Disable unsupported union preaggregation unless an independent implementation and parity proof establish correctness. Never use rendered marks, sampled points or pixels as the complete evidence population.
recommendations.benefit: Prevents apparently fast interactions from producing incorrect records or written claims.
recommendations.cost: Exact rechecking can consume some or all of the preview speed benefit; union falls back to the exact path. This correctness cost must be measured, not hidden.

impact.exactness: Exact ID equality remains mandatory; approximation cannot be justified by matching a visible aggregate or count.
impact.performance: May limit acceleration eligibility and reduce speedups near boundaries; measured fallback is preferable to incorrect evidence.
impact.public_api: Any preview/approximation distinction must be explicit. Do not expose an 'exact' API backed solely by quantized membership.

recommendations.alternative: Use the exact unoptimized predicate path for all committed selections and reserve pixel binning solely for display.

confidence.basis: The difference between source membership and quantized intervals is demonstrable by a small static example, and the paper states the resolution restriction.
confidence.caveat: No upstream runtime defect or speed penalty was measured.

requirements: Compare original and accelerated stable ID sets just below, on and above every relevant boundary, including the 20.9 counterexample.
Verify preview, committed result, CSV, trace and written finding use the declared exactness policy.
For any union candidate, test two nonempty overlapping/disjoint clauses with optimization on/off; otherwise require exact fallback.
Measure boundary rechecking and candidate expansion cost separately.
stop_conditions: Immediate NO-GO on a single exact-membership mismatch or on unsupported union acceleration presented as correct.

recommendations.title: Avoid a general Boolean editor, report DSL or framework rewrite
recommendations.problem: A general selection/report/query framework would expand the project far beyond the concrete lasso and selected-count need. It would add APIs and ambiguous combinations before proving user benefit.
affected_workflow: Add a small authored data-bound statement

evidence.locator: prompt.md: Verified local starting facts; Ranked questions 1–3
evidence.claim: The assignment calls for a small direct design, no speculative framework, no default general Boolean editor, and no generated prose/arbitrary code/report template language.
Current intent favors a bounded lasso and one selected-count binding.
Broad named population management has low priority and should wait for a concrete task.

recommendations.proposed_change: Limit the first contract to the primitive predicates and one exact geometry kind required by the proof; add correlated tuples only when a real task requires them. Keep resolution policies few and explicit. Bind one count in authored content without arbitrary expressions or generated text. Reject enterprise layers, server infrastructure and renderer/framework replacement as prerequisites.
recommendations.benefit: Keeps the feature understandable, reviewable and useful within the project's intended scale.
recommendations.cost: Lower initial and ongoing API/maintenance cost; some advanced composition requests remain deliberately unsupported.

impact.exactness: A smaller supported surface makes complete membership and lifecycle proof more attainable.
impact.performance: Avoids speculative infrastructure and unmeasured abstraction overhead; no runtime improvement is guaranteed.
impact.public_api: Deliberately constrains the public surface and avoids a general user-authored execution/query language.

recommendations.alternative: Revisit one specific additional operation or binding only after a demonstrated workflow cannot be expressed safely with the bounded contract.

confidence.basis: The scope limitation is explicitly required and reinforced by current intent briefs.
confidence.caveat: Future requests may justify individual extensions; this recommendation does not prohibit them categorically.

requirements: Show that the bounded four-consumer workflow is useful without a backend or general authoring language.
For each new syntax/node/UI control, identify the concrete task and exact membership proof it enables.
Keep unsupported combinations visible and nonwidening rather than inventing implicit semantics.
stop_conditions: Stop scope expansion that has no demonstrated task or introduces unresolved Boolean, denominator or population meaning.

recommendations.title: Make source-facet and population scope explicit at new interaction boundaries
recommendations.problem: A selection made inside a local population or facet can emit a global field condition, while other interactions select exact source contributors. Both meanings can be useful, but they must not be described as the same selected records.
affected_workflow: Select within a facet or chart-local population

evidence.claim: Source chart populations restrict displayed/context rows without automatically becoming outgoing interactive predicates.
Ordinary field intervals and exact density contributor-ID selections can carry different source-population meanings.
Facet IDs and facet guards enter different paths explicitly; they cannot be inferred from a source view label alone.
Notebook mode clears cross-chart dimensions while retaining workspace predicates; it does not create one implicit notebook-selected cohort.
The recorded intent accepts current global-coordinate behavior; a new scope rule must not silently change that existing interaction.

recommendations.proposed_change: Start the common four-consumer proof with an un-faceted shared population. For new scoped interactions, choose explicitly between a global field predicate and contributors within the source population/facet, record that meaning in provenance, and apply target-local restrictions separately. Preserve existing accepted global-coordinate behavior. A notebook finding that follows one chart needs an explicit source binding; workspace-only consumers keep their workspace scope.
recommendations.benefit: Makes apparent cross-view differences explainable and prevents selecting unseen sibling rows while claiming to select only source contributors.
recommendations.cost: Small-to-moderate scope/provenance work and targeted duplicate-coordinate/facet tests; avoid a named population management UI.

impact.exactness: Defines which exact population each target should resolve instead of forcing unlike scopes to have equal counts.
impact.performance: Additional scope predicates may add evaluation work; measure only after correctness is established.
impact.public_api: Prefer internal explicit target policy first. Expose a user-facing scope choice only when the interaction needs it, without changing legacy defaults silently.

recommendations.alternative: Keep global field selection as the sole new supported policy initially, clearly label it, and defer facet-contributor selection until a concrete task requires it.

confidence.basis: The existing local-population and outgoing-predicate separation is explicit in source.
confidence.caveat: Which new interaction should use contributor scope is a product choice; stop rather than guess if the proof requires an unresolved choice.

requirements: Use equal x/y values in two facets/populations and assert the declared global or source-contributor IDs for every target.
Test source context exclusion separately from facet/local-population restrictions.
Distinguish absent scope from an explicit empty facet set.
Verify notebook local selection never silently filters siblings while workspace constraints still apply.
stop_conditions: Stop on silently inherited source scope, scope widening, empty-scope reinterpretation or an unresolved product choice.

recommendations.title: Require docs, reachable demos, keyboard operation and semantic gates at each milestone
recommendations.problem: A technically plausible resolver is not complete if users cannot understand its scope, operate or clear it, inspect evidence, recover with history, or find a working example. A passing benchmark cannot substitute for these semantic and workflow checks.
affected_workflow: Discover and operate the new interaction
Read scope and inspect exact evidence

evidence.locator: prompt.md: Ranked question 5; Deliverables and evidence rules
evidence.claim: Every user-visible milestone requires docs and a demo; semantic acceptance is separate from optional acceleration, and future UI checks include keyboard and wide/intermediate/narrow widths.
Current work should preserve an uninterrupted evidence/recovery task and extend only a concrete capability.
Existing table interaction has keyboard and focus contracts to preserve.
History remounts preserve focus and global undo avoids editable targets/dialogs.
Desktop support and existing UI conventions should remain explicit; narrow resilience checks do not automatically create a new mobile support promise.

recommendations.proposed_change: Tie each user-visible milestone to an updated filters/selection or narrative docs section and a reachable deterministic demo. Keep the existing four-consumer example structure and delivered Heatmap examples as regressions. Require keyboard-equivalent selection/inspection, Escape cancellation/clear, visible scope/status, focus recovery and wide/intermediate/narrow checks. Report every proposed check as unrun until Codex executes it, and gate acceleration separately.
recommendations.benefit: Makes exactness understandable and usable, preserves accessibility/recovery, and leaves a reviewable path from research to integration.
recommendations.cost: Bounded documentation, demo registration and workflow QA for each milestone; this is completion work, not a new documentation or UI framework.

impact.exactness: Row-ID, trace, denominator and export gates remain the primary acceptance criteria.
impact.performance: Performance gates are additional and optional; no speed result can override semantic failure.
impact.public_api: Document any actual new persisted/API behavior and supported viewport limits without promising speculative compatibility.

recommendations.alternative: Keep the feature as an internal research-only spike if documentation, demonstration or semantic/keyboard acceptance cannot yet be completed.

confidence.basis: These completion requirements are explicit in the assignment and current trust intent.
confidence.caveat: All new product/UI/performance checks remain proposed and unrun in this research.

requirements: Complete the named docs section and reachable demo for every user-visible milestone.
Pass exact IDs, trace contributors, finding/count, complete CSV, clear/undo/restore and lifecycle checks before optional acceleration gates.
Exercise keyboard operation, focus, cancel/clear, read-only preview and note-editor undo ownership.
Verify wide/intermediate/narrow layouts expose scope, status and evidence actions; record the desktop support limitation.
Record executed versus unrun checks and stop/GO/defer decisions with evidence.
stop_conditions: Do not call a milestone complete with only screenshots, aggregate agreement, a benchmark, or an undocumented pointer-only interaction.
